title: Help making this tileset work in MV

posts.author: VHStapes
posts.body:
Hey everyone! I bought a tileset and I need help resizing it and putting it into the right format for MV. I tried posting it and a link to it in another forum here and the post got rejected with no explanation, so I'm weary of posting it or the link here again, but if this post gets approved maybe someone can let me know how I should go about posting it? I would happily pay a few bucks to someone to format the tiles for me correctly, I am just fully stumped. Thank you!
You can find it
here
(posting apprehensively but I figure y'all will need to see it somehow). I can send it over via google drive link if someone is willing to help, and I can follow directions well if someone wants to tell me what to do. Thanks!

posts.body:

maybe someone can let me know how I should go about posting it?
Click to expand...
most artists forbid reposting their work, especially if it is commercial usable.
so postings of resources not your own will often get deleted.
you need to link to them instead, and in the case of shop resources you'll have to link to the shop page of the work.

Click to expand...
Hi
@VHStapes
, it's not complicated, but you'll need a little patience:
MV's tilesets are 768x768 pixel .png files, one tile is 48x48 which gives you a grid of 16x16 tiles.
1) resize your images:
your images are 16x16 pixel size tiles, so you need to triple the image size for 48x48 tiles.
To do this, I use photofiltre (which is very easy to learn) but you can use whatever you want ^^.
Spoiler:
If you use photofiltre
Be careful, in the "resize image" tool, there's "sampling method", don't use the default "automatic" mode as it will blur your image quite ugly, use the "closest" mode.
2) Reorganize the tiles:
Now that you've resized your images, you need to recover the elements you're interested in and integrate them into a 16x16 grid of 48x48 pixels.
when doing this, always save everything in .png format to avoid any loss of quality/transparency/etc...
Spoiler:
If you use photofiltre
to save your work in progress, always save as .pfi. It's not the image but your work file that will keep everything, with layers etc., so that if you need to make a modification it's much easier to keep this file.
use template grids to stick things on easily, like this :
https://invenblocker.tumblr.com/post/161891747018/templates-for-rpg-maker-mv-tilesets-in-order-a1

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
So, since they are name your own price I just downloaded them to see the issue.
They are 100% not in RPG maker format - doesn't mean they aren't convertible, but you have to understand how the format works, be able to edit them and set them up. What you do for these is:
(I use GIMP and Graphicsgale for editing here, both free)
Open all 4 files in Gimp, depending if you want transparent or not, just choose the according ones.
Under image, scale image, scale them by 300% without interpolation:
With a combination of "View - show grid", "Image - configure grid (where you set it to 48x48)" and "View - snap to grid" you make it easier to copy and paste.
Create a new 768 x 768 sized image and repeat the grid related steps. Now you copy (or cut) and paste everything from those 4 sheets onto that new one - each cell in the grid just into a new one. You can copy in batch, just make sure nothing overlaps or is "outside" of the picture. Once your image is full, make a new one and fill it with the rest.
!Make sure the upper left tile on each sheet is empty, the maker interprets that one differently!
So here is how creatures could be pasted into that format:
How you organize them does not matter, you bascially have B, C, D, E as slots, so four sheets the engine allows and you can fit everything onto two or three with quite some gaps, so no need for perfect oganisation.
But what about the autotiles? They are simply not set up to work out of the box in the format MV uses. The edges need to fit into a 24x24 square, and that isn't the case for these. Maybe there is an engine that has the format the tiles you have in this set use, but RPG Maker is not it. You can use them on a B/C/D/E sheet or even copy them onto an A5 sheet if you want them on a bottom layer.
You can convert them into autotiles, but that requires understanding of the autotile format.
So, for this, I opened the file in graphicsgale, used "all frames - resample" and then 300% and unchecked smooth to upscale the sheet. You can do that in gimp to, I find graphicsgale here more convenient.
Use a 24x24 grid and start assembling your autotile like this:
1. copy the "one tile all outer edge" and "one tile all inner" next to each other:
Copy those four outer edges below, just with the offset you see here:
Piece the middle parts in from here:
Why you need to use those "narrow" strips? because the MV autotiles achieves all those different curves you have in the provided autotile as well, but those are made out al individual 48x48 tiles, not dynamically places 24x24 pieces. That means, your tiles have to be more flexible. That means, the resulting autotile here works (you can place it onto an A2 sheet in the right place), but has less shape variation.
I personally would do both, make conversions and map with the "not autotile autotile individual pieces" if I want that look.
